question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{2x-{x}^{5}}{{x}^{3}+5} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{2x}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}-{x}^{2})}{(1+\frac{5}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{0-{x}^{2}}{1-0} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,{x}^{2} \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
